newsitem.title: USA: Ross projects Q2 drop in revenues.
newsitem.headline: Ross projects Q2 drop in revenues.

text.p: ROSS Technology Inc said Thursday that it expected its second quarter results from operations to come in lower than analysts' estimates, citing a sharp decline in revenues from its microprocessor chip customers.
The company said it expected to post net revenues for the quarter, which ends September 30, in the mid-$20 million range. It said there was a possibility it would record a "modest" operating loss.
ROSS Technology attributed the bulk of the decline to a "sharper-than-expected" drop in microprocessor chip customers.
The company said it expects revenues from microprocessor chips for the quarter to come in at about $14 million, compared with about $20 million in the first fiscal quarter.

It said the revenue decline is "directly attributable" to an 85 percent drop between quarters in sales to computer maker Sun Microsystems Inc. It said such sales to other ROSS customers have not declined.

The company did not provide projected earnings per share. For the second quarter, analysts have estimated the company will post earnings per share of $0.17, the same level it reported in the first quarter, and a drop from the 1996 second quarter's $0.22 per share.
A company spokesman did not immediately return a telephone call seeking more information.
